$comment: RENDER FIXTURE for DecisionScreen — supplied by WP-2.3, which the fixture register named as
the work package that would clear its entry.
WHY THIS IS NOT THE HARNESS INVENTING AN ENGINE OUTPUT.
The register's objection was that a verdict is an ENGINE OUTPUT, and contract §1 forbids P2
from computing judgements — so the render harness could not manufacture one on the fly without
inventing precisely the thing P2 may not derive.
A committed fixture is a different act. It is test data, it lives under __tests__, it is
reviewable in a diff, and it is labelled as an input rather than presented as a finding. The
harness still passes EMPTY params to every other screen; only a screen with a declared fixture
gets one, and the declaration is what a reviewer checks.
WHAT THE VALUES ARE FOR. `verdict` selects a label and a colour class — nothing computes from
it. `reason` is present so the screen renders the ENGINE-REASON path; the refusal path that
replaced VERDICT_FALLBACK_REASONS is exercised by the absence of this field, which is why the
`fxComparison` is deliberately EMPTY. Populating it would put fabricated FX percentages on a
rendered screen, which is the defect D6 just removed from this very file.

default.reason: FIXTURE — not an engine output. Present so the screen renders its engine-reason path.

noEngineReason.$why: Exercises the D6 refusal path: with no reason, the screen must say no reason arrived rather than substitute a per-verdict sentence.
